item.title: Management Consultant – Transportation Access & Coordination (Federal)
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/18/2026.

Note: 3 years of public sector consulting experience required. Salary $74,000–$124,000. Ability to obtain Public Trust clearance required. No travel required. Location: Washington, DC area (confirm via Guidehouse). Familiarity with human services transportation, non-emergency medical transportation, and transportation access a plus.

Guidehouse seeks a Management Consultant to support a team addressing an Executive Order, legislative requirements, and Federal agency objectives around transportation access and coordination for underserved populations. The Consultant will own the development and quality of client products, work with a team to establish and manage work plans, deadlines, and deliverable requirements, directly manage client relationships, and collaborate across Federal agencies to find opportunities for better transportation coordination. Washington, DC area. Salary $74,000–$124,000.

Key responsibilities include: working with federal clients and team members to develop the strategic planning process and manage implementation activities for an interagency council; planning, drafting, and developing products such as outreach and communications materials, strategic plan components, executive-level meeting presentations, and public-facing transportation resources on behalf of a federal client; developing facilitation guides, talking points, and materials for federal executives for webinars, presentations, and meetings; supporting and leading client interactions including meeting preparation, facilitation, and follow-up while maintaining strong client relationships; and collaborating across federal offices and agencies, identifying opportunities to improve transportation-related coordination and efficiency.

Qualifications: a bachelor’s degree; 3 years of public sector consulting experience; experience with creating and refining public sector policy initiatives; experience conducting research and collecting data through qualitative (interviews, focus groups) and quantitative means and writing executive-level reports with keen attention to detail; experience with project management and facilitation and consensus building; experience in working with and delivering communications to senior level audiences; and advanced proficiency in the full Microsoft suite (PowerPoint, Teams, SharePoint) and Google Workspace suite (Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive). Ability to obtain Public Trust clearance required. Preferred: familiarity with federal agencies, policies, and programs; familiarity with public transportation particularly human services transportation, non-emergency medical transportation, and transportation access.

Compensation and logistics: salary $74,000–$124,000. Comprehensive Guidehouse benefits including medical, dental, vision, parental leave, 401(k), life and disability, HSA/FSA, STD/LTD, student loan paydown, tuition reimbursement, and mobility stipend. Ability to obtain Public Trust clearance required. No travel required.

item.title: Management Consultant – Federal Programs & Program Management (DHS focus)
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/18/2026.

Note: 2+ years of professional experience supporting federal clients in a consulting firm required. Salary $74,000–$124,000. Must obtain and maintain DHS Public Trust (candidates with active Public Trust or suitability preferred). Up to 10% travel. Location: Washington, DC area. Preferred backgrounds include public policy, government, international studies, accounting, finance, business, IT, computer science, audit readiness, data science, communications, and STEM.

Guidehouse’s Management Consulting professionals help clients identify, evaluate, and solve some of their most complex challenges, assisting them in achieving their strategic goals and objectives to fulfill their mission. Guidehouse seeks a Management Consultant to support government agencies on a diverse set of project-specific tasks covering a broad set of program and project management consulting capabilities. Washington, DC area. Salary $74,000–$124,000.

Key responsibilities include: assisting clients in designing, developing, launching, and improving new projects and programs focused on achieving their strategic goals, objectives, and mission; assisting clients to identify, develop, and implement performance metrics and measurement tools to monitor program performance and evaluate whether programs are achieving their goals; assisting clients in analyzing projects and programs to identify risks and help develop, apply, and monitor mitigations; documenting and evaluating business processes and making recommendations for process improvements; applying a variety of analytical, problem-solving, and reporting skills and techniques; producing a variety of communications from informal email interactions to formal memos, issue papers, presentations, and executive briefings; conducting research to investigate client problems and collaborating with the team to formulate and recommend solutions; supporting clients in collecting and analyzing data, producing models and visualizations, and drawing conclusions from data to improve decision-making; and analyzing and helping develop and/or improve policies and procedures for a variety of programs and operational needs. Additionally: assisting in business development activities, developing learning and development materials, and supporting recruiting.

Qualifications: must be able to obtain and maintain a DHS Public Trust; a bachelor’s degree; 2+ years of professional experience supporting federal clients in a consulting firm with strong analytical and communications skills. Preferred backgrounds: public policy, government, international studies, accounting, finance, business, IT, computer science, audit readiness, data science, communications, STEM; knowledge of project management principles; experience working in teams to produce high-impact work products in a fast-paced environment; and desire to support public sector clients with a national security mission.

Compensation and logistics: salary $74,000–$124,000. Comprehensive Guidehouse benefits including medical, dental, vision, parental leave, 401(k), life and disability, HSA/FSA, STD/LTD, student loan paydown, tuition reimbursement, and mobility stipend. Must obtain DHS Public Trust clearance. Up to 10% travel.

item.title: Government Relations Coordinator
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/18/2026.

Note: Professional experience in a legislative setting or in government relations is a plus (not required). Salary $56,000–$75,000. Hybrid in Washington, DC area (minimum 3 days/week in-office, Monday–Wednesday required; must live in MD, DC, or VA). Overnight and out-of-state travel required including to twice-yearly conferences. Apply via 340B Health Career Center with resume and cover letter.

340B Health assists safety-net hospitals to provide services to more patients with low incomes and those living in rural areas, focusing on protecting the federal 340B drug pricing program so it continues to play its critical role of subsidizing the health care safety net. 340B Health seeks a Government Relations Coordinator to support efforts to shape strategies and tactics to effectively represent the organization on Capitol Hill, with the administration, and throughout the 340B provider community. The GR Coordinator will play an integral role in government relations activities and collaborate with 340B Health member hospitals to engage in advocacy. Washington, DC area (hybrid). Salary $56,000–$75,000.

Key responsibilities include: assisting the Director of Grassroots in executing two lobby day events per year for member hospitals including event logistics, program and materials preparation, participant recruitment, and post-event analysis and follow-up; maintaining GR team calendars and coordinating meeting invitations; arranging and supporting meetings and calls with members, outside consultants, and other stakeholders; assisting the Director of Grassroots in working with member hospitals to develop and share with policymakers the impact 340B has on their hospitals and patients; monitoring and informing staff via the government relations platform of 340B activity on Capitol Hill including legislation, hearings, and other congressional activity impacting the 340B program; assisting the Director of Grassroots in administering the Champions Recognition Program; updating content and maintaining the association’s Federal Advocacy Toolkit web content; supporting and contributing to government relations projects including newsletters, webinars, and action alerts; maintaining the government relations database; attending and assisting with bi-annual conferences; and assisting with developing and editing government relations’ written material including talking points, policy summaries, PowerPoint presentations for lobby days, and government relations webinars.

Qualifications: a bachelor’s degree required; professional experience in a legislative setting or in government relations is a plus; strong writing and communication skills; strong skill in attention to detail; knowledge of Congress and the legislative process preferred; commitment to schedules, deadlines, and high-quality work product; strong organizational and time management skills; and experience using the Microsoft Office suite (Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint). Must live in MD, DC, or VA. Overnight and out-of-state travel required. Must be able to occasionally lift and carry light materials up to 25 pounds.

Compensation and logistics: salary $56,000–$75,000 based on experience. Exceptional compensation package including health, dental, life insurance, disability insurance, paid time off, and retirement plan matching. Hybrid in Washington, DC area (minimum 3 days/week in-office, Monday–Wednesday required). Must live in MD, DC, or VA. Twice-yearly out-of-state conferences required. Apply via 340B Health Career Center with resume and cover letter.

item.title: Sr. Analyst, Public Policy – Cybersecurity & Technology
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/18/2026.

Note: 5 years of relevant professional experience required in public policy, government affairs, cybersecurity or technology policy, national security, or a related field. Salary $70,000–$115,000 plus bonuses, equity grants, and comprehensive benefits. Strong preference for candidates based in DC/MD/VA (multiple days/week in office required). Exceptional candidates in San Francisco, Austin, or NYC also considered. Occasional travel. No visa sponsorship mentioned — confirm with employer.

CrowdStrike is a global leader in cybersecurity protecting people, processes, and technologies with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. CrowdStrike seeks a Sr. Analyst, Public Policy to join its global Public Policy team, supporting work across a range of cybersecurity, technology, and digital policy issues with a particular focus on U.S. public policy and policy partnerships. The role approximately splits time 50% on policy-related work, 25% on internal-facing compliance, and 25% on administrative and organizational support for the public policy team. DC/MD/VA area strongly preferred. Salary $70,000–$115,000.

Key responsibilities include: preparing regular internal policy updates, news summaries, legislative and regulatory trackers, meeting readouts, and other materials that keep the Public Policy team and key internal stakeholders informed of relevant developments; supporting internal Public Policy compliance; conducting research and supporting the preparation of memos, backgrounders, talking points, briefing materials, presentations, and other written products for Public Policy team members and other CrowdStrike leaders; maintaining organizational tools to manage the team’s policy partnerships and external engagements leveraging AI tools where appropriate; supporting the team’s day-to-day meeting and engagement workflow including scheduling and coordinating meetings, preparing agendas and background materials, managing logistics, taking notes, and tracking follow-up items; and assisting with the preparation and coordination of policy events, conferences, roundtables, and other external engagements.

Qualifications: 5 years of relevant professional experience in public policy, government affairs, cybersecurity or technology policy, national security, or a related field; a bachelor’s degree in a relevant topic (public policy, international relations, national security, security studies, cybersecurity, political science, or a related discipline); demonstrated interest in cybersecurity, AI, and technology policy; excellent research, analytical, and writing skills; strong judgment and attention to detail; strong organizational, project-management, and administrative skills; and proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows, and drive business outcomes. Preferred: advanced degree in a relevant field; experience working in or with the U.S. federal government, Congress, a state government, policy research organization, trade association, or technology company.

Compensation and logistics: salary $70,000–$115,000 plus eligibility for bonuses and equity grants. Comprehensive CrowdStrike benefits including market-leading compensation, comprehensive physical and mental wellness programs, competitive vacation and holidays, paid parental and adoption leaves, and professional development opportunities. DC/MD/VA area strongly preferred. Occasional travel. Great Place to Work Certified.

item.title: Research Analyst – Behavioral Health Policy
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/18/2026.

Note: Master’s degree in public policy or a social science discipline OR bachelor’s in public policy or a social science discipline and 2–5 years of relevant experience required. Salary $58,500–$77,000. Hybrid preferred (Bethesda, MD or other Westat office, 2 days/week). U.S. citizenship required by contract. No H-1B visa sponsorship. Employee-owned (ESOP). Note: This is a different and more junior posting from WESTAT-BHRESASSOC (master’s required, $69K–$92K) already in the feed.

Westat is a leader in research, data collection and analysis, technical assistance, evaluation, and communications. Westat seeks a Research Analyst to join its team supporting continued work on behavioral health and health policy, assisting with projects that address the needs of individuals with mental health conditions and substance use disorders. The Research Analyst will work closely with project leadership and multi-disciplinary project teams to help translate science into resources for diverse audiences including federal and state policy makers, clinical service providers, and individuals affected by mental health conditions and substance use disorders. Hybrid preferred (Bethesda, MD). Salary $58,500–$77,000.

Key responsibilities include: supporting all stages of research from study design through data collection and management, analysis, and report writing; conducting literature searches, synthesizing research findings, and contributing to writing on health policy and behavioral health topics; assisting in synthesizing research findings; conducting data collection efforts such as administering surveys, interviews, site visits, and observation protocols and acquiring administrative data; providing technical assistance and training to federal grantees and other stakeholders; presenting evaluation findings to federal clients and other stakeholders; and assisting with analysis of qualitative or quantitative data.

Qualifications: a master’s degree in public policy or a social science discipline (sociology, economics, political science, psychology) or in analytical methods such as applied statistics — OR a bachelor’s degree in public policy or a social science discipline and 2–5 years of relevant experience; experience with quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods evaluation approaches and using analytic software; experience using Microsoft Office software to produce reports, tables, graphs, and presentation slides; experience creating data visualizations; U.S. citizenship required by contract. Preferred: experience writing technical reports or contributing to peer-reviewed journal articles; knowledge of public health approaches to evaluate mental health conditions and substance use disorders; experience using library databases and reference management tools; experience working on federal government contracts especially for SAMHSA. No H-1B visa sponsorship.

Compensation and logistics: salary $58,500–$77,000. Comprehensive Westat benefits including ESOP, 401(k), paid parental leave, 15 vacation days, 9 sick days, 7 government holidays and 2 floating holidays, professional development, and medical, dental, vision, STD/LTD, life and AD&D. Hybrid preferred (Bethesda, MD or other Westat office, 2 days/week). U.S. citizenship required. No H-1B visa sponsorship. Posting open for minimum 5 days (rolling).

item.title: Program Manager / Senior Program Manager – Children, Youth & Families
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/18/2026.

Note: Grant-funded position — continued employment contingent on funding availability. 3 years minimum required. Salary: Program Manager $70,000–$85,000; Senior Program Manager $85,000–$93,000 (level determined by qualifications). Hybrid at NACo offices (Washington, DC area; confirm hybrid schedule with NACo). Bachelor’s required (advanced degree preferred). 4–6 trips per year for travel. Focus on prenatal-to-three (PN3) policies, childcare, and maternal health.

The National Association of Counties (NACo) is the national organization representing all 3,069 U.S. counties. NACo seeks a Program Manager (or Senior Program Manager based on experience) for its Children, Youth and Families educational programming activities in the County Practices and Innovations department. The role focuses on timely execution of project-based deliverables, producing and disseminating best practice content, and hosting impactful small group events for county officials around prenatal-to-three (PN3) policies, childcare, and maternal health. Washington, DC area (hybrid). Salary $70,000–$93,000.

Key responsibilities include: leading day-to-day execution and project management for NACo’s children, youth and families educational programming activities by providing strategic and content expertise and managing the timely delivery and quality of deliverables for project activities related to PN3 policies, childcare, and maternal health; designing and executing virtual and in-person events (webinars, conference workshops, multi-day events) with responsibility for content planning, logistics coordination, and post-event follow-up; promoting and liaising with the Counties for Kids network — an active community of practice for county leaders interested in PN3, childcare, and/or maternal health; researching best practices and developing educational resources such as case studies, toolkits, and issue briefs; maintaining productive ongoing relationships with county elected officials, maternal and infant health leaders, state associations of counties, philanthropic organizations, state and federal agency partners, researchers, and national associations; and advising NACo partners on county roles and authorities in children, youth, and families.

Additional Senior Program Manager responsibilities include: managing initiative budget activities including forecasting, monitoring, and ensuring adherence to program budgets; hiring and overseeing consultant contracts; supervising up to two program interns as needed; and identifying relevant funding opportunities and leading proposal development for future children, youth and families programs.

Qualifications: minimum 3 years of experience in early childhood, public policy, local government, or foundation sectors; a bachelor’s degree required (advanced degree preferred) in early childhood, maternal and infant health, public policy, public administration, or a related field; strong project management and organizational skills; excellent verbal and written communication skills including public speaking and conducting formal meetings; ability to work well in a political environment while maintaining a nonpartisan perspective; and ability to work well with individuals from ideologically, racially, ethnically, and socioeconomically diverse backgrounds. Preferred: experience working with or for local government; experience working with or for a membership organization; advanced degree or relevant certification; and project management certification. Grant-funded — contingent on funding availability. 4–6 trips per year.

Compensation and logistics: salary $70,000–$85,000 (Program Manager) or $85,000–$93,000 (Senior Program Manager) based on qualifications. Comprehensive NACo benefits. Hybrid (Washington, DC area). 4–6 trips per year. Grant-funded — contingent on funding availability. Level determined by selected candidate’s qualifications and experience.

item.title: Public Affairs Specialist (GS-1035-11/12) – DOJ
item.description:
⚠️ Application deadline: November 5, 2026 — TODAY. Apply immediately via USAJOBS. USA Hire assessment required within 48 hours of application submission. Must meet all qualification requirements by 11/05/2026.

Note: GS-11: 1 year specialized experience at GS-9 equivalent required (or Ph.D./3 years of higher graduate education). GS-12: 1 year specialized experience at GS-11 equivalent required. U.S. citizenship or national required. Drug screening required. Background investigation required. USA Hire assessment required within 48 hours of closing date. Resume must clearly support responses to the online questionnaire. Apply via USAJOBS.

The U.S. Department of Justice seeks a Public Affairs Specialist (GS-1035-11/12) to deal with a myriad of entities including print, radio, television, internet media, law enforcement agencies, government officials, and private industry; advise and assist departmental components on communications strategies and resolving issues to align public affairs messaging across the Department; and represent the organization in media interviews, press conferences, and stakeholder meetings.

Key responsibilities include: advising and assisting other departmental components on communications strategies and resolving issues to align public affairs messaging; developing and maintaining thorough knowledge of Department policies, guidelines, and internal regulations; evaluating program effectiveness, advising leadership, and recommending modifications; organizing and coordinating media interviews with Department leadership and developing supporting materials; organizing press conferences and other media events to enhance the Department’s law enforcement initiatives; responding in writing and/or orally to information requests from the media, specialized groups, and the general public; using traditional and social media content to monitor and analyze news stories that directly affect the Department; representing the organization in media interviews and press conferences with agency officials, government representatives, and stakeholder associations; and establishing and maintaining effective relationships with media representatives, Department stakeholders, and across the public affairs community.

Qualifications (GS-11): 1 year of specialized experience at GS-9 equivalent including (1) assisting in planning or managing public relations programs; (2) conducting research in response to media inquiries; and (3) drafting content for news releases, fact sheets, informational pieces, or talking points — OR Ph.D./3 full years of progressively higher graduate education in a related field — OR combination. (GS-12): 1 year of specialized experience at GS-11 equivalent including (1) advising organization management or decision-makers on public affairs matters; (2) representing an organization in an official capacity during media interviews, press conferences, or meetings; and (3) responding to inquiries from members of the news media. USA Hire assessment required within 48 hours of closing date. 1-year probationary period required (fitness for public interest evaluated).

Compensation and logistics: salary at GS-11/12 locality pay (confirm via USAJOBS/DOJ). Comprehensive federal benefits. Apply via USAJOBS by November 5, 2026 — TODAY. USA Hire assessment required within 48 hours of submission.

item.company: Booz Allen Hamilton – Navy Data & AI Governance
item.title: Data and AI Policy & Governance Analyst – Navy (Secret)
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/18/2026.

Note: Active Secret clearance required. HS diploma or GED minimum (bachelor’s preferred). Salary $86,800–$198,000. Navy data and AI policy, governance, and cloud migration focus. Posting closes within 90 days. 5+ years of experience with data architecture preferred.

Booz Allen Hamilton seeks a Data and Artificial Intelligence Policy and Governance Analyst to support the planning, development, implementation, and oversight of Navy data and AI initiatives including policy, governance, cloud migration, data-center compliance, and enterprise implementation efforts. The Analyst will facilitate the development and implementation of the Navy’s data and AI policies, ensuring strict alignment with Department of Navy and Department of War Chief Data and AI Office Strategies. Active Secret clearance required. Salary $86,800–$198,000.

Key responsibilities include: coordinating project execution by tracking milestones, risk, and deliverables and maintaining integrated roadmaps; supporting cloud migration and data-management initiatives; facilitating the development and implementation of the Navy’s data and AI policies, ensuring strict alignment with Department of Navy and Department of War Chief Data and AI Office Strategies; planning and leading Data and AI Governance forums, working groups, and stakeholder meetings and documenting decisions and coordinating stakeholder participation in AI initiatives; and preparing senior-level briefs and decision materials while managing collaboration repositories and collaborative workspaces using M365 tools.

Qualifications: experience supporting project, program, portfolio, or organizational-management activities; experience with data management, data governance, artificial intelligence, cloud migration, digital modernization, or related enterprise IT initiatives; experience with the Microsoft 365 environment including Microsoft Teams, SharePoint Online, Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint; ability to develop concise executive briefings, status reports, and meeting materials; active Secret clearance required; HS diploma or GED required. Preferred: 5+ years of experience with data architecture; experience supporting senior-level meetings, working groups, and decision-making forums; experience with project management; experience with Power Apps; and a bachelor’s degree.

Compensation and logistics: salary $86,800–$198,000. Comprehensive Booz Allen benefits. Active Secret required. Posting closes within 90 days.

item.company: Office of Management and Budget (OMB) – Executive Office of the President
item.title: Program Examiner – Agriculture & Interior (GS-9 to GS-15)
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/18/2026.

Note: Multiple grade levels available (GS-9 through GS-15). Direct Hire Authority — veterans preference and traditional rating and ranking do not apply. U.S. citizenship required. Drug testing required. Security clearance required. Must meet all qualification requirements by the closing date. Candidates with an active clearance preferred. Salary at applicable GS grade and DC locality pay (confirm via USAJOBS/OMB). Probationary period may be required (fitness for public interest evaluated). Resumes shared with additional federal agencies unless candidate opts out. Apply via USAJOBS (search OMB Program Examiner Agriculture Interior).

The Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Executive Office of the President, seeks Program Examiners for major Federal program portfolios covering Agriculture and Interior, directing qualitative and quantitative analyses supporting formulation, presentation, execution, and oversight of the President’s Budget. Program Examiners lead analyses of sensitive and cross-cutting Federal program, budget, legislative, regulatory, financial management, procurement, and organizational issues with Administration or government-wide implications. This is one of the most substantive budget and policy analyst roles in the federal government. Multiple grade levels. Direct Hire Authority.

Key responsibilities (full performance): serving as a senior Program Examiner and advisor for major Federal program portfolios; leading analyses of sensitive and cross-cutting Federal program, budget, legislative, regulatory, financial management, procurement, and organizational issues with Administration or government-wide implications; formulating and recommending funding levels, resource allocations, policy alternatives, legislative or regulatory approaches, management reforms, and other actions affecting major Federal programs and national priorities; developing and presenting decision memoranda, issue papers, briefings, and recommendations for senior OMB officials, Executive Office of the President leadership, and other executive decision makers; leading or playing a principal role in negotiations, interagency working groups, and high-level meetings; and resolving conflicting positions and representing OMB on potentially controversial matters.

Qualifications: GS-9: 1 year at GS-7 equivalent gathering and researching information concerning programs, budgets, or organizational operations and assisting in preparing written reports or briefings — OR master’s degree/2 full years of graduate education — OR combination. GS-11: 1 year at GS-9 equivalent including analyzing information, collaborating in development of analytical products, and communicating with stakeholders — OR Ph.D./3 years of graduate education — OR combination. GS-12 through GS-15: progressively more complex specialized experience as described in the USAJOBS announcement. U.S. citizenship required. Direct Hire Authority — all qualified applicants forwarded to selecting official.

Compensation and logistics: salary at applicable GS grade (GS-9 through GS-15) with DC locality pay (confirm via USAJOBS/OMB). Comprehensive EOP/federal benefits. Washington, DC. Direct Hire Authority — veterans preference and traditional ranking do not apply. Drug testing required. Security clearance required. Probationary period may be required. Apply via USAJOBS. Resumes may be shared with additional federal agencies unless candidate opts out.

item.company: Public Citizen – Climate Program / Texas Office
item.title: Organizer/Lobbyist – Texas Corporate Immunity Campaign (Climate)
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/18/2026.

Note: 2–5 years of relevant experience in organizing and advocacy required. Salary $72,919–$105,513 plus generous benefits. One-year grant-contingent position with possibility of renewal. Texas-based (Austin area and statewide). Some travel required. Submit cover letter, resume, and writing sample to climateaction@citizen.org. Women, people of color, LGBTQ+, and multilingual speakers encouraged to apply.

Public Citizen is a national, non-partisan, public interest group with more than 1,000,000 members and supporters that holds the government and corporations accountable on issues including money in politics, open government, financial regulation, energy and the climate crisis, fair trade, consumer protection, access to justice, tax policy, workplace safety, drug and medical device safety, healthcare, and more. Public Citizen’s Climate Program and Texas office seek an organizer to support efforts to block anticipated legislation that would take away the legal tools Texas communities use to hold corporations accountable for harmful misconduct. Texas-based. Salary $72,919–$105,513.

Key responsibilities include (Organizing and Advocacy): identifying opportunities where direct action organizing, grassroots advocacy, and traditional as well as out-of-the-box earned media tactics can make a difference; building a coalition effort in support of the anti-immunity campaign including traditional and nontraditional (conservative-leaning) allies; and identifying and developing the leadership of local spokespersons. (Media and Public Education): developing and maintaining media relationships and responding to press inquiries; helping develop media strategies; writing editorial board memoranda, press releases, op-eds, letters to the editor, and blog posts; and representing Public Citizen in public forums. (Lobby the Legislature): identifying and tracking priority legislation; lobbying key lawmakers and staff; educating allies about legislation and opportunities; driving public communications to legislative staff about priorities; and organizing trips to Austin to provide in-person testimony at committee hearings. Making things happen: developing materials, recruiting partners, holding meetings, working with coalitions, and organizing events to win.

Qualifications: 2–5 years of relevant experience in organizing and advocacy; strong strategic thinking and oral and written communication abilities; outstanding people skills with proven ability to build relationships and get volunteers and partners invested for the long term; high energy, enthusiasm, persistence, and attention to detail; ability to work independently, balance multiple priorities, and react to new developments under pressure; creative and collaborative spirit; and strong commitment to the cause. Knowledge or experience on climate and energy policy in Texas, organizing in Texas, and lobbying the Texas legislature is a plus. Some travel required.

Compensation and logistics: salary $72,919–$105,513. Generous benefits including medical, vision, and dental (100% paid by Public Citizen, including full coverage for children); three weeks paid vacation plus five personal days; 401(k) with 5% contribution from Public Citizen after one year; 12 weeks of paid parental leave after one year; sabbatical after 8 years; student loan reimbursement program. Texas-based. One-year grant-contingent position with possibility of renewal. Submit cover letter, resume, and writing sample to climateaction@citizen.org.

item.title: Business Process Transformation Consultant – Federal (Active Secret)
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/18/2026.

Note: Active and maintained Secret clearance required. 3+ years of professional experience in consulting, business analysis, business process mapping, or technology delivery required. Salary $98,000–$163,000. Must work on client site in Arlington, VA 3–5 times per week. No travel beyond the client site.

Guidehouse seeks a Business Process Transformation Consultant to support modernization of management services for a Federal agency by identifying services for business process reengineering, implementing operational excellence through assessments and process improvement, and driving data-driven decision making. Arlington, VA (3–5 days/week at client site). Salary $98,000–$163,000. Active Secret required.

Key responsibilities include: conducting ‘as-is’ and ‘to-be’ business process analysis to document workflows, identify inefficiencies, and recommend optimized future-state processes; reengineering and standardizing processes to reduce redundancies, improve cycle time, and streamline decision-making; creating or enhancing dashboards, KPIs, and decision-support reporting for senior leaders; applying data analytics to drive efficiency, cost, and time savings and improve customer experience through communication, knowledge sharing, training, and process improvements; facilitating leadership and team workshops to assess current state, define future state, and develop goal-based strategic, operational, and tactical plans; and conducting program analysis, market research, opinion polling, and benchmarking and producing reports, briefings, and actionable recommendations.

Qualifications: an active and maintained Secret clearance; a bachelor’s degree; 3+ years of professional experience in consulting, business analysis, business process mapping, or technology delivery; and ability to work on client site in Arlington, VA 3–5 times per week. Preferred: experience facilitating or co-facilitating stakeholder meetings and/or workshops; familiarity with digital transformation, AI/ML initiatives, or process automation; exposure to Power BI, Tableau, or similar data visualization tools; Lean Six Sigma certification or experience supporting continuous improvement projects; and experience documenting business processes or requirements and producing client-facing deliverables.

Compensation and logistics: salary $98,000–$163,000. Comprehensive Guidehouse benefits including medical, dental, vision, parental leave, 401(k), life and disability, HSA/FSA, STD/LTD, student loan paydown, tuition reimbursement, and mobility stipend. Active Secret required. Arlington, VA (3–5 days/week onsite).

item.title: Outreach Analyst – National Security & Public-Private Engagement (Secret)
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/18/2026.

Note: Minimum Secret clearance required. Bachelor’s and strong academic record required. Salary $60,000. Shortlisted candidates must submit a 10–15-page writing sample. item.title: White House Fellows Program – 2027–2028 Class
item.description:
Note: Application deadline January 14, 2027 (letters of recommendation due January 21, 2027). Submit application via whitehousefellows.gov using Login.gov. U.S. citizenship required. Undergraduate degree completion required by application deadline (graduate degree not required). Most federal employees are not eligible (exceptions: career military personnel and some special government employees). No age restriction. Active-duty military applicants must obtain required permission. TS/SCI clearance eligibility required (dual citizens may apply). Fellows receive a competitive federal salary during the program year. Washington, DC (year-long, full-time commitment).

The White House Fellows Program is one of America’s most prestigious programs for leadership and public service. Founded in 1964, the program has a nonpartisan tradition and has operated under both Republican and Democratic administrations. White House Fellows are selected by the President’s Commission on White House Fellowships to serve for one year in paid federal service working with a senior government principal, with an educational program complementing the placement through discussions with leaders and study of public policy in practice. Applications for the 2027–2028 class are open. Application deadline January 14, 2027.

The selection process is competitive. Former Fellows screen applications to identify the most promising candidates, and the most qualified applicants are selected to be interviewed by regional panels. Approximately 30 candidates proceed as National Finalists; the President’s Commission then interviews and recommends 11–19 outstanding candidates for a one-year presidential appointment. National Finalists are subject to investigation and verification by accredited federal investigators. Fellows must be eligible to obtain a top-secret security clearance.

The application consists of three parts: Part 1 (personal information, contact details, eligibility information, current employment, declarations); Part 2 (education, employment, and civic/volunteer experience; six essays covering current employment (200 words), most significant professional achievement (200 words), most significant community service achievement (200 words), lifetime goals (300 words), motivation for becoming a White House Fellow (300 words), and a 500-word memorandum for the President); and Part 3 (three letters of recommendation, with an optional fourth). Fellows receive a competitive federal salary, are eligible for Federal Employee Health Benefits, and are responsible for their own housing arrangements in Washington, DC. All activities are mandatory; the program year is a full-time commitment. Fellows may not receive outside salary or hold positions in outside organizations during the fellowship year.

Compensation and logistics: competitive federal salary. Federal Employee Health Benefit Plans available through placement agency. Washington, DC (year-long, full-time, mandatory commitment). U.S. citizenship required. Undergraduate degree required by application deadline. Must be eligible for TS/SCI clearance. Application deadline January 14, 2027. Apply at whitehousefellows.gov.

This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/11/2026.

Note: This is a part-time contractor/internship position (~10 hours/week) at $25/hour. 1099 contract position — no benefits. In-person in Washington, DC near Dupont Circle. Availability on Tuesday and/or Thursday evenings highly preferred. Enrollment in a bachelor's or master's program highly preferred.

PAVE (Parents Amplifying Voices in Education) is a nonprofit organization connecting, informing, and empowering parent leaders to give families in DC a voice and choice in the vision for education. PAVE seeks a Policy and Advocacy Intern to support the team in amplifying its voice, streamlining projects, and ensuring effective organizational operations. Washington, DC (in-person near Dupont Circle). $25/hour, ~10 hours/week.

Key responsibilities include (Legislative Monitoring, Research, and Analysis): tracking local and national legislation relevant to education, family engagement, equity, and parent advocacy; summarizing bills, hearings, and votes in concise, parent-accessible language; supporting research and analysis of various topics, organizations, and key players in the education field; assisting with the collection, aggregation, and analysis of community feedback data; and creating policy and advocacy content for PAVE including informational materials, slide decks, reports, and materials for parent-centered policy and advocacy curriculum. (Project Coordination and Event Support): assisting with project planning and event coordination across teams and providing logistical support for events and meetings. (Operations Support): helping maintain calendars, contact lists, and shared files.

Qualifications: high school diploma or GED required; current enrollment in a bachelor's or master's program in education, policy, business, communications, writing, or nonprofit management highly preferred; strong writing and editing skills with ability to adapt to different voices and audiences; excellent organizational skills; and experience with Microsoft and Google Suite. Basic design skills (Canva or similar) preferred. Availability on Tuesday and/or Thursday evenings highly preferred.

Compensation and logistics: $25/hour, ~10 hours/week. 1099 contractor position — no benefits. W-9 required prior to employment. In-person in Washington, DC near Dupont Circle. Occasional evening and weekend events.

item.company: OMB – Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA)
item.title: Policy Analyst (GS-9/11/12) – OIRA/OMB
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/11/2026.

Note: Direct Hire Public Notice — traditional rating, ranking, and veterans’ preference do not apply. Multiple grade levels (GS-9, GS-11, GS-12) based on qualifications. U.S. citizenship required. Security clearance required. Drug testing required. Washington, DC. More than one selection may be made within 90 days. Apply via USAJOBS.

The Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA), within the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) in the Executive Office of the President, is the nation’s central regulatory review authority. OIRA Policy Analysts work on matters pertaining to the regulatory and information policies of federal department and agency missions across areas including tax policy, financial services, banking, consumer protection, food safety, health, education, income maintenance, labor, transportation, justice, and security. Washington, DC.

Key responsibilities include: conducting analyses of Executive Branch regulations and regulatory policies to identify and work with EOP officials and promulgating agencies to address significant regulatory, economic, legal, scientific, and privacy issues; reviewing information collection requests to ensure they meet all requirements under the Paperwork Reduction Act; coordinating and reviewing actions submitted to OIRA under Executive Orders 12866, 14192, and 14215; working on policy issues in collaboration with staff and senior career and policy officials from across the EOP (e.g., the Council on Environmental Quality, the Domestic Policy Council, the National Economic Council, the National Security Council) and the broader Executive Branch; collaborating with staff to develop written products and make oral presentations for high-level decision makers that summarize and provide analytically based recommendations on regulatory and policy matters; developing relationships with regulatory experts at covered agencies; coordinating with colleagues from across OIRA and OMB on privacy, statistical policy, science policy, economics, and budget matters; reviewing agency compliance with the Paperwork Reduction Act, Privacy Act, Information Quality Act, Congressional Review Act, and other criteria; and reviewing Congressional testimonies, Statements of Administration Policy, Questions for the Record from Congress, and other official statements.

Qualifications (GS-9): 1 year of specialized experience at GS-7 demonstrating (1) assisting with analyzing or reviewing regulatory or policy proposals using economic, legal, or policy analysis frameworks and (2) assisting with developing materials to present policy or regulatory ideas, conclusions, or recommendations — OR a master’s degree or equivalent, 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education, or LL.B. or J.D., or a combination. (GS-11): 1 year at GS-9 demonstrating (1) synthesizing regulatory or policy proposals and (2) developing policy or regulatory recommendations to be reviewed by higher-ranking staff — OR a Ph.D. or equivalent, or 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education, or LL.M., or a combination. (GS-12): 1 year at GS-11 demonstrating (1) analyzing, reviewing, or developing regulatory or policy proposals, (2) recommending policy or regulatory conclusions, and (3) collecting, organizing, or synthesizing quantitative or qualitative data used in development of regulations or policy. U.S. citizenship required. Security clearance required. Drug testing required.

Compensation and logistics: salary per GS-9/11/12 pay scale, Washington DC locality (confirm via USAJOBS). Comprehensive federal benefits. Washington, DC. Direct Hire Public Notice — multiple selections may be made. Apply via USAJOBS.

item.title: Junior International Labor Analyst
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/11/2026.

Note: Fully onsite at U.S. Department of Labor in Washington, DC (occasional meetings at ICF’s Rockville, MD office). Bachelor’s degree required. 2+ years of experience required. U.S. citizenship required; must have resided in the U.S. for the past 2 years (for low-level security clearance). No H-1B visa sponsorship. Salary 3,770–25,408. Apply directly via ICF — do not use AI to generate interview responses (ICF policy).

ICF is a global advisory and technology services provider. ICF seeks a Junior International Labor Analyst to support work with the U.S. Department of Labor (USDOL) Office of Child Labor, Forced Labor and Human Trafficking (OCFT). On behalf of OCFT, ICF conducts research, analysis, and preparation of written communications related to international child labor, forced labor, human trafficking, trade, and supply chain issues. The role coordinates between USDOL, U.S. Government agencies, nongovernmental organizations, and regional and international organizations. Fully onsite at USDOL, Washington, DC. Salary 3,770–25,408.

Key responsibilities include: applying knowledge of quantitative and qualitative research methods to conduct systematic and objective inquiry and analysis of international child labor, forced labor, and human trafficking issues; performing data collection from existing global and local sources and conducting library and computer research; formulating strategies to engage with relevant country stakeholders based on USDOL and U.S. priorities and examining policy issues with a long-term perspective; coordinating between elements of USDOL, U.S. Government agencies, nongovernmental organizations, and regional and international organizations; and writing in a clear, concise, organized, and convincing manner tailored for the intended audience.

Qualifications: a bachelor’s degree in international affairs, public policy, economics, international development, political science, communications, planning, statistics, technology and policy, or a related discipline; 2+ years of experience working on research related to forced labor, child labor, or human trafficking; U.S. citizenship required; must have resided in the U.S. for the past 2 years (ability to obtain low-level security clearance); and no H-1B visa sponsorship. Experience writing policy reports for U.S. Government agencies and experience with supply chain tracing preferred.

Compensation and logistics: salary 3,770–25,408. Comprehensive ICF benefits. Fully onsite at USDOL, Washington, DC (occasional meetings in Rockville, MD). U.S. citizenship required. No H-1B visa sponsorship. Apply directly via ICF’s website.

item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/11/2026.

IMPORTANT: This position is NOT open to the general public. Eligible applicants include: current DoW or DoWEA civilian employees, ICTAP/CTAP eligibles, VEOA-eligible veterans, military spouses (E.O. 13473), OPM Interchange Agreement eligibles, Non-DoW transfers, and Priority Placement Program eligibles. Note: GS-14. Secret (Tier 3) clearance required. 1 year of specialized experience at GS-13 equivalent required. Multiple DoW locations. On-call 24/7 for serious or high-visibility incidents. 1-year probationary period required.

The Department of War (DoW) seeks a GS-14 Policy Analyst to develop and implement policies and procedures for casualty reporting, mortuary affairs, and Military Funeral Honors programs. The role analyzes casualty reporting and mortuary affairs support plans, advises senior officials on policy and procedural changes, and influences representatives of diverse organizations to reach consensus on significant matters impacting service members and their families. Multiple DoW locations.

Key responsibilities include: reviewing assigned programs for potential efficiencies based on joint service initiatives and/or federal partnership opportunities; developing policies and procedures within DoW for casualty, mortuary affairs, and Military Funeral Honors; defending proposed program efforts involving these areas; influencing representatives of diverse organizations to reach consensus on significant matters impacting service members and/or their families; managing, coordinating, and facilitating the flow of information between parties; analyzing casualty reporting and casualty assistance support to ensure compliance with policy and to make recommendations for improvement; interpreting and applying existing law and regulations to a wide range of issues involving casualty, mortuary affairs, and Military Funeral Honors; and analyzing mortuary affairs support plans and field operations.

Qualifications: 1 year of specialized experience at GS-13 equivalent including analyzing policies and procedures involving casualty, mortuary affairs, and/or Military Funeral Honors; developing such policies and procedures; developing strategic plans for implementation and/or administration of policy; advising senior officials on policy or procedural changes; and developing position papers, decision memos, and/or training materials. Secret (Tier 3) clearance required. U.S. citizenship required. Must be eligible under one of the limited appointment authorities listed above.

Compensation and logistics: salary per GS-14 pay scale with applicable locality pay (confirm via USAJOBS). Comprehensive federal benefits. Multiple DoW locations. item.title: Long Term Care (LTC) Fellow
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/10/2026.

Note: Part-time (50% time / ~20 hours/week), 2-year fellowship. Compensation 0,000/year. Contract position — no benefits. Remote. Graduate degree or equivalent required. 3–10 years of experience required. IMPORTANT: Must apply exclusively by email to LTCFellow@economicsecurityproject.org. Do not apply through job board websites (LinkedIn, Indeed, ZipRecruiter, etc.).

The Economic Security Project (ESP) seeks a Long Term Care (LTC) Fellow to build out a new body of work situating long-term care within ESP’s broader affordability agenda. ESP is a leading progressive economic policy and advocacy organization working on issues of economic power, affordability, and security. This is a half-time, two-year fellowship (~20 hours/week) for someone who wants to develop original policy research and help shape a growing area of ESP’s platform. The Fellow will map the long-term care policy landscape, author a flagship policy paper connecting LTC to ESP’s affordability framework, and help integrate long-term care into existing campaigns. Remote. Compensation 0,000/year.

Key responsibilities include (Year 1): researching and writing a flagship policy paper situating long-term care within ESP’s affordability framework, with actionable policy recommendations; supporting development of ESP’s health care platform including policy memos, briefs, and talking points that integrate long-term care into ESP’s broader health reform arguments; representing ESP in relevant coalition spaces including the Affordability Campaigns Collaborative and other priority external tables, and building new coalition partnerships; and helping represent and support ESP in amplifying LTC in the popular discussion through op-eds, social media, and media interviews. (Year 2): helping plan and execute a major convening bringing together long-term care policy experts, health reform advocates, and policymakers; and authoring a second campaign-facing research product or policy brief building on year-one research.

Qualifications: a graduate degree or equivalent knowledge and experience in a relevant field (e.g., economics, law, sociology, public policy); 3–10 years of experience in policy research, analysis, or advocacy, ideally touching health care, long-term care, aging policy, and/or economic security; strong analytical and writing skills with the ability to translate research into clear, persuasive material for policy and public audiences; comfort engaging directly with coalition partners, advocacy organizations, and policymakers; self-directed and able to manage a multi-year research project with minimal day-to-day oversight; and familiarity with Medicaid, Medicare, and/or long-term care policy.

Compensation and logistics: 0,000/year. Contract position — no benefits. 50% time (~20 hours/week). 2-year term. Remote. Reports to the Director of Cash Initiatives. IMPORTANT: Apply exclusively by emailing resume and one-page cover letter to LTCFellow@economicsecurityproject.org. Do not apply through job board websites.

item.title: FSOC Junior Fellowship (GS-9, 2027)
item.description:
Application deadline: November 15, 2026. Apply by emailing cover letter, resume (≤2 pages), writing sample, one letter of recommendation, and transcript(s) to FSOCRecruitment@treasury.gov. Contact the same address with questions or requests for assistance.

Note: 2-year fixed term. GS-9 level. U.S. citizenship required (must be able to provide documentation). Preference given to recent undergraduates. Resume must demonstrate 52 weeks (2,080 hours) of relevant paid or unpaid work, volunteer, or extracurricular experience. Start date summer 2027 (or mutually agreed alternative). Applications evaluated December 2026; finalists asked to respond to two short essay questions.

The Financial Stability Oversight Council (FSOC) Junior Fellowship is a selective, fixed two-year program for new college graduates to work at the Office of the Financial Stability Oversight Council — the interagency body within the U.S. Department of the Treasury responsible for monitoring and maintaining United States financial stability. Junior Fellows have exposure to multiple policy issues and opportunities to enhance their knowledge and skills, working alongside senior officials at Treasury and FSOC member agencies. Washington, DC. GS-9 level.

Key responsibilities include: coordinating FSOC’s interagency committees and working groups; analyzing domestic economic and financial developments and financial stability risks; examining financial market data; helping to develop policy recommendations; and supporting meetings of the Council and its working groups and committees, including engagement with senior officials at Treasury and FSOC member agencies.

Qualifications: recently received or will soon receive a bachelor’s degree with relevant coursework in economics, public policy, finance, international relations, or related fields; strong candidates will demonstrate 52 weeks (2,080 hours) of relevant paid or unpaid work, volunteer, or extracurricular experience relevant to the duties described above; and U.S. citizenship required. Preference is given to undergraduates due to the structure of the program. Note veterans’ preference in application if applicable.

Compensation and logistics: GS-9 level salary (Washington, DC locality; confirm via OPM GS pay table). Standard Treasury benefits. 2-year fixed term. Start date summer 2027 (or mutually agreed alternative). Application deadline November 15, 2026. Apply by email to FSOCRecruitment@treasury.gov with cover letter, resume (≤2 pages, including time period and average hours/week for each role), writing sample, one letter of recommendation, and transcript(s). Applications evaluated December 2026.

item.title: Summer Associate Program 2027 (SAC & STPI)
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/7/2026.

Note: Paid summer program — minimum 10 weeks, core period early June through end of July 2027. Must be returning to an academic institution in fall 2027 (not graduating). Preference for graduate students; rising seniors considered. Security investigation required — applicants must be eligible for access to classified information. Criminal background check required. Pay 0.50–2.00/hour. Alexandria, VA. Resume and transcripts required. Apply via Handshake or IDA’s website.

The Institute for Defense Analyses (IDA) is a not-for-profit corporation operating Federally Funded Research and Development Centers (FFRDCs) that provide objective analyses of national security issues to the U.S. government. IDA’s Summer Associate Program provides students with a unique opportunity to use their quantitative and analytic skills to work on challenging real-world national security issues. Two FFRDCs are accepting Summer Associates for Summer 2027: the IDA Systems and Analyses Center (SAC) and the IDA Science and Technology Policy Institute (STPI), which assists the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy and other executive branch agencies in formulating federal S&T policy. Pay 0.50–2.00/hour. Alexandria, VA.

SAC is comprised of seven research divisions covering cost analysis, global dynamics and intelligence, information technology and systems, joint advanced warfighting, operational evaluation, strategy forces and resources, and science/systems/sustainment. Responsibilities vary depending on division and particular assignment.

Qualifications: highly qualified students with strong academic backgrounds; preference for graduate students, but rising seniors returning to school in fall 2027 will be considered. SAC seeks disciplines including computer science, information technology, mathematics, chemistry, physics, operations research, engineering, materials science, statistics, economics, social and behavioral sciences, human resources, security, international relations, policy studies, finance, data science, AI, machine learning, library and information science, English, and history. STPI seeks disciplines including behavioral sciences, biological sciences, computer science, economics, engineering, environmental sciences, learning sciences, mathematics, physical sciences, social sciences, and statistics. Security investigation required; must be eligible for classified information access. Criminal background check required. Resume and transcripts required.

Compensation and logistics: pay 0.50–2.00/hour. Associates responsible for living expenses during the summer. Minimum 10 weeks; core period early June through end of July 2027. Alexandria, VA. Apply via Handshake or IDA’s website; submit resume and transcripts.

Safe Shores – The DC Children’s Advocacy Center provides survivor-centered intervention, hope, and healing for children and families affected by abuse, trauma, and violence in the District of Columbia. The Youth Advocacy Initiative (YAI) Coordinator provides administrative support and coordination of services within the Youth Advocacy Initiative, working to ensure the smooth daily operation of YAI services. The role also involves direct client support and on-call advocacy during after-hours shifts. This position is a mandated reporter for child abuse and neglect under DC law. Washington, DC (fully on-site).

Key responsibilities include (Program Coordination and Administration): maintaining and ensuring quality and confidentiality of electronic records, statistical tracking, and inventory; tracking participant attendance and program outcomes, assisting with grant reporting, and supporting YAI program budget management; supporting writing, reviewing, editing, and updating desk manuals, SOPs, and internal and external training guides; managing and stocking supplies at primary service delivery locations; maintaining, organizing, and restocking the youth clothing closet; purchasing, tracking, distributing, and auditing Emergency Victim of Crime Funds (EVCF) and gift cards for emergency client assistance; ensuring daily program coverage; and drafting and reviewing narrative reports for OVSJG and other government funding sources. (Direct Client Support and On-Call Advocacy): providing crisis intervention and advocacy support to teens ages 13–17 (and family as desired) during the initial medical and/or law enforcement response to sexual assault during on-call shifts; providing information to teenagers about available support, service resources, victims’ rights, and the multidisciplinary team investigation process; coordinating with other involved service providers or government agencies in accordance with the Sexual Assault Victims’ Rights Amendment Act of 2019; and providing accompaniment to teens and/or their families for hospital visits and law enforcement interviews during on-call shifts. Qualifications: a bachelor’s degree, preferably in a human services-related field such as Social Work, Psychology, Counseling, or related disciplines; experience in program or project management, administrative or clerical responsibilities, budget oversight, inventory management, and/or event planning; advanced proficiency using data systems to track client and program metrics; knowledge of Microsoft environment and SharePoint; and strong public speaking skills. At least 1 year of professional experience with youth and families and at least 1 year of direct client engagement or case management experience preferred. Criminal background check and Child Protection Registry clearance required.

Compensation and logistics: salary not stated (confirm via Safe Shores/Idealist). Washington, DC (fully on-site). On-call rotation required including after-hours, holidays, and weekends. Mandated reporter. Criminal background check and Child Protection Registry clearance required.

Note: Active Secret security clearance required (ability to obtain). PhD preferred; master’s + 2 years minimum. Three programs currently hiring within RSP. Arlington, VA.

CNA’s Regional, Strategy and Policy Analysis (RSP) Division provides senior national security decision-makers with regional and global analysis linking strategy, policy, and operations. Three programs are currently hiring Research Analysts: (1) Ally and Partner Security Affairs (APA) — analyzing foreign government strategies, operations, and capabilities; expertise sought in allied navies and joint forces, strategic laydown and posture, and regional expertise on NATO and the Indian Ocean region. (2) Countering Threats and Challenges (CTC) — analyzing future conflict, force design, asymmetric warfare, and adversary dynamics; expertise sought in force design, net assessment, asymmetric warfare, Russia studies, and future operating environment. (3) Strategy and Policy Analysis (SPA) — analyzing national security and defense strategy challenges; expertise sought in strategic and nuclear deterrence, defense strategy, emerging technology integration, and naval campaigning in multiple regions.

Key responsibilities include: developing sound analytic frameworks and methodologies for addressing both structured and unstructured problems; making significant contributions to research publications and analytic products for individual projects; communicating results clearly in writing and presentations to colleagues, sponsors, and external audiences; and building and maintaining strong client relationships.

Qualifications: minimum master’s degree in International Relations, International Affairs, Public Policy, Political Science, Security Studies, or a relevant field (PhD preferred); PhD & 0+ years or master’s & 2+ years of experience in research and analysis; strong analytic curiosity and creativity; excellent interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills; and ability to obtain and maintain an Active Secret security clearance.

Compensation and logistics: salary competitive (confirm via CNA). Comprehensive CNA benefits. Arlington, VA. Active Secret clearance required. Deadline: November 30, 2026.

item.company: HHS ASPE – Office of Science and Data Policy (ORISE)
item.title: Health Policy Research Fellow (ORISE)
item.description:
Application deadline: December 1, 2026 at 3:00 PM ET. A complete application must include an application, transcripts, a current resume/CV, and one educational or professional recommendation. Apply via the ORISE opportunity portal (reference code HHS-ASPE-2026-0004-B). All documents must be in English.

Note: This is a paid ORISE fellowship — participants do not become employees of HHS, DOE, or ORISE. Monthly stipend + healthcare stipend. U.S. citizens and Lawful Permanent Residents only. Master’s or doctoral degree in economics or related field required (received within the past five years). Appointment initially for one year, may be renewed based on funding.

The HHS Office of the Assistant Secretary for Planning and Evaluation (ASPE) has fellowship opportunities available in the Office of Science and Data Policy. ASPE advises the HHS Secretary on policy development, leads special initiatives, coordinates the Department’s evaluation, research, and demonstration activities, and manages cross-Department planning activities. The selected fellow will be mentored by a team of economic, policy, and public health experts focusing on healthcare markets, with opportunities to train on a wide range of data resources, collaborate on research studies, and engage in quantitative and qualitative analytical projects supporting ASPE priorities. Washington, DC.

Learning objectives include: developing and maintaining subject matter expertise in rural healthcare systems, Medicaid policy, and Health Insurance Marketplace financing and eligibility frameworks; analyzing regulations, legislation, executive directives, and policy reports; conducting and supporting research and program evaluation activities; synthesizing complex policy information into clear, actionable insights; drafting professional correspondence, policy briefs, reports, presentations, and talking points; and communicating policy analysis and research findings in support of strategic briefings for HHS leadership.

Qualifications: master’s or doctoral degree in economics or a related field received within the past five years; experience designing, planning, conducting, and communicating the results of analytical projects; and knowledge of and experience with methodological and statistical techniques for analyzing and interpreting relevant data.

Compensation and logistics: monthly stipend commensurate with educational level and experience, plus a healthcare stipend. Washington, DC. ORISE fellowship (not federal employment). U.S. citizens and LPRs only. Appointment initially for one year, may be renewed. Application deadline: December 1, 2026 at 3:00 PM ET.

item.title: Young Professionals Programme (YPP) – Development & Sustainability
item.description:
Application period: October–November 2026. Apply via inspira.un.org. The 2026 application window is now open.

Note: This is a competitive examination program, not a direct hire. Successful candidates are placed on a roster for P-1 or P-2 level positions — placement on the roster does not guarantee an offer of employment. For 2026, the United States is a participating country for the Development and Sustainability exam area only. Must be 32 years of age or younger (born on or after January 1, 1994). Must be willing to serve at any UN duty station worldwide. Attach a government-issued photo ID and degree documentation to your application.

The UN Young Professionals Programme (YPP) is a recruitment initiative for talented professionals to start a career as an international civil servant with the UN Secretariat. The examination process consists of a two-stage online written exam followed by a competency-based video-conference interview. Successful candidates are placed on a roster valid for three years from which they are selected to fill appropriate vacancies at UN offices worldwide (including Addis Ababa, Bangkok, Beirut, Geneva, Nairobi, New York, Santiago, and Vienna). Successful candidates receive a two-year fixed-term contract at the P-1 or P-2 level, with the possibility of a continuing contract after two years subject to satisfactory performance.

Estimated timeline: Application period October–November → Applications screened December–January → Assessment process February–May → Interviews and results June–August. Note: timeline varies year to year.

The YPP exam has two online stages: Stage 1 consists of approximately 2 hours of multiple choice questions (general and specialized), available in English or French. Stage 2 consists of approximately 2–2.5 hours of specialized constructed-response questions; may be proctored remotely. Candidates successful in both stages are invited to a competency-based video-conference interview.

Eligibility requirements: nationality of a participating Member State (U.S. eligible for Development & Sustainability exam area in 2026); a bachelor's degree or equivalent (at least a 3-year degree) relevant to the exam area; 32 years of age or younger in 2026 (born on or after January 1, 1994); fluency in English or French (UN Level II proficiency required in all four areas — speaking, reading, writing, and understanding).

Compensation and logistics: P-1 or P-2 level UN salary scale (competitive international civil service compensation including benefits and allowances — confirm current rates via careers.un.org). 2-year fixed-term contract. Placement at any UN duty station worldwide. Application via inspira.un.org. Application period: October–November 2026.

item.company: CDC – Public Health Informatics Fellowship Program
item.title: Public Health Informatics Fellow (Class of 2027)
item.description:
Application deadline: November 6, 2026. Application period opened September 1, 2026. Apply via the CDC PHIFP application portal.

Note: This is a 2-year paid fellowship, not a federal government employment position. Fellows are placed in assignments at CDC centers, institutes, and offices (CIOs) across CDC. Stipend amount not stated — confirm via the CDC PHIFP website.

The CDC Public Health Informatics Fellowship Program (PHIFP) trains professionals in the systematic application of knowledge about systems that capture, manage, analyze, and use information to improve population-level health outcomes. The Class of 2027 fellowship provides on-the-job training for professionals to apply expertise in computer science, data analytics, and data science to public health. Fellows are assigned to host sites within CDC where they work on advanced projects to enhance information systems and data projects to improve the nation's health. Based at CDC in Atlanta, GA.

The fellowship provides a two-year, competency-based training in public health informatics, consisting of 90% on-the-job training and 10% coursework in informatics, data science, and public health. Required activities include: working on public health informatics projects within the assigned host site; providing short-term technical assistance to federal, international, state, local, and territorial health departments and nonprofit agencies through special requests (Info-Aids); and designing, developing, implementing, enhancing, or evaluating an information system or artifact in the public health domain (capstone project). Fellows also attend a two-week orientation at the start of the program.

Day-to-day activities include: working with teams involved in research and development of public health information systems; conducting informatics evaluations on complex public health information systems; contributing to CDC's emergency response activities; and providing technical assistance to state and local health departments and international public health agencies through short-term assignments.

Qualifications: background in computer science, data analytics, data science, or a related field; interest in applying technical expertise to public health challenges. See the CDC PHIFP website for complete eligibility requirements.

Compensation and logistics: paid fellowship (stipend amount not stated; confirm via CDC PHIFP website). 2-year program. Based at CDC, Atlanta, GA. Application deadline: November 6, 2026.
