item.company: Asian Pacific American Institute for Congressional Studies (APAICS)
item.title: Congressional Fellowship 2027-2028
item.description:
Application deadline: December 18, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. A completed application must include: a cover letter expressing interest in the program; a one-page maximum resume; an academic transcript; two letters of recommendation (submitted by recommenders directly via the APAICS portal by December 18); and responses to three written questions (each no more than one page, double-spaced, 12-point Times New Roman font).

Note: APAICS Congressional Fellows are not employees of the federal government, their host office, or APAICS. Fellows receive a monthly educational stipend. Program dates: August 30, 2027–August 25, 2028. Washington, DC. This fellowship has a focus on Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander (AAPI) communities and public policy.

The Asian Pacific American Institute for Congressional Studies (APAICS) Congressional Fellowship offers individuals the opportunity to serve our nation and deepen their understanding of public policy through participation in the legislative process. Fellows are placed with a congressional office or committee for 12 months and are given work equivalent to that of a congressional legislative aide. By the end of the fellowship, fellows will have established a professional network on Capitol Hill, understand how Congress operates, and acquired skills and expertise that make them marketable to congressional offices, federal agencies, nonprofits, and the private sector.

Each fellowship experience will differ depending on the office in which fellows are placed and the portfolio assigned; however, fellows gather as a cohort twice a month to discuss their experiences and for professional development opportunities. Fellows are also expected to attend APAICS-organized events including the Annual Awards Gala and policy summits, and must make a public presentation on a policy topic of their choosing toward the end of the fellowship year.

The three written questions ask applicants to: (1) describe how they envision the APAICS fellowship playing a role in their career path and what they hope to gain; (2) describe their experience in the U.S. with AAPI communities and how proximity to or distance from these communities has shaped their views on public policy; and (3) describe a time when they worked as part of a team and encountered a challenge.

Compensation and logistics: monthly educational stipend (amount not stated; confirm via APAICS). 12-month fellowship. Washington, DC. Program dates: August 30, 2027–August 25, 2028. Application deadline: December 18, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET.

item.title: Postgraduate Fellowship 2027-2028
item.description:
Application deadline: December 1, 2026. Apply via the CHCI website at chci.org.

Note: This is a paid, 9-month fellowship. A master's degree or JD completed within two years of the August 2027 program start date is required (i.e., degree completed after approximately August 2025). Program dates: August 18, 2027–May 19, 2028. Washington, DC. This fellowship is designed for emerging Latino leaders and individuals deeply committed to the Latino community.

The Congressional Hispanic Caucus Institute (CHCI) Postgraduate Fellowship Program offers emerging Latino leaders and individuals deeply committed to the Latino community the opportunity to draw connections between their graduate field of study and public policy. This paid, nine-month fellowship allows fellows to spend four days per week on Capitol Hill obtaining unparalleled work experience and exposure to the legislative process, and one day per week in leadership development programming centered on CHCI's four Pillars of Leadership. Fellows also organize and host a Capitol Hill briefing on a policy topic and publish an issue brief with CHCI.

Available fellowship concentrations include: Child Welfare, Health, Housing, Education, Law, Technology, and Transportation.

Program requirements include: working a minimum of 32 hours per week at a placement site; attending a 9-day orientation and weekly leadership development sessions throughout the program; completing community service hours; participating in all CHCI-sponsored activities including Hispanic Heritage Month events, summits, and receptions; researching, writing, and publishing an issue brief on a topic that impacts the Latino community within the fellowship discipline; planning, developing, and executing a policy briefing on Capitol Hill; and complying with CHCI policies regarding work performance and personal conduct.

Qualifications: a master's degree in any field or JD completed within two years of the August 2027 program start date.

Compensation and logistics: paid fellowship (stipend amount not stated; confirm via chci.org). 9-month program, August 18, 2027–May 19, 2028. Four days/week Capitol Hill placement; one day/week leadership development. Washington, DC. Application deadline: December 1, 2026.

item.title: Health Policy Fellowship (ORISE)
item.description:
A fellowship opportunity is available in the Office of Health Policy within the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Planning and Evaluation (ASPE) at the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) in Washington, DC. Note: this is an ORISE-administered fellowship (administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy). Participants do not become employees of HHS, DOE, or the program administrator -- this is a stipend, not a salary, and there are no employment-related benefits. U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent residency required. A master's or doctoral degree received within the past 5 years is required. Applications reviewed on a rolling basis; final deadline December 1, 2026.

The selected fellow will be mentored by a team of economic, policy, and public health experts who focus on healthcare markets, and will have opportunities to train with a wide range of data resources, collaborate on research studies, and engage in both quantitative and qualitative analytical projects in support of ASPE's priorities. Learning objectives include: developing and maintaining subject matter expertise in rural healthcare systems, Medicaid policy, and Health Insurance Marketplace financing and eligibility frameworks; analyzing regulations, legislation, executive directives, and policy reports; conducting and supporting research and program evaluation activities; synthesizing complex policy information into clear, actionable insights; and drafting professional correspondence, policy briefs, reports, presentations, and talking points.

Qualifications: a master's or doctoral degree in a relevant field (social science or related) received within the past five years; experience designing, planning, conducting, and communicating the results of analytical projects within economics or related fields; and knowledge of and experience with methodological and statistical techniques. The office has particular interest in applicants with experience in demography or actuarial science (not required). U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent residency required.

Compensation and logistics: monthly stipend commensurate with educational level and experience; stipend for healthcare benefits (not employer-sponsored benefits). One-year initial appointment, may be renewed contingent on funding. Full-time. Based in Washington, DC. Application deadline: December 1, 2026 (rolling reviews).
